title: Binet's Formula and Lamé's 5-Digit Bound
description: Proves Lamé's 5-digit bound without restriction (euclideanSteps(a,b) ≤ 5·decimalDigits(b) for all b > 0) and Binet's formula fib(n) = (φⁿ - ψⁿ)/√5. Part I: the five-step Fibonacci identity fib(5k+7) ≥ 10·fib(5k+2) implies fib(5k+2) ≥ 10^k. Part II: Binet's formula via paired induction, with φ⁵ > 10 explaining why 5 digits correspond to one Euclidean step. 21 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Lamé's 1844 theorem was the first analysis of algorithm complexity: the Euclidean algorithm on b requires at most 5·⌊log₁₀(b)⌋ + 1 steps. The connection to Fibonacci numbers is classical: the worst case is consecutive Fibonacci numbers, and Fibonacci numbers grow like φⁿ/√5 by Binet's formula (1843). This file formalizes both the unrestricted 5-digit bound and the deeper golden ratio explanation.
overview.problemStatement: Prove (1) fib(5k+2) ≥ 10^k for all k (no restriction on k), giving the unrestricted Lamé bound; (2) Binet's formula fib(n) = (φⁿ - ψⁿ)/√5; (3) φ⁵ > 10, explaining why 5 decimal digits correspond to one Euclidean step.
overview.text:
Part I: The five-step identity fib(5k+7) = 8·fib(5k+2) + 5·fib(5k+1) with fib monotone gives fib(5k+7) ≥ 10·fib(5k+2). By induction, fib(5k+2) ≥ 10^k. Since b < 10^(⌊log₁₀b⌋+1) ≤ fib(5(⌊log₁₀b⌋+1)+2), the parent module's lame_step_bound gives the result.

Part II (Binet namespace): φ = (1+√5)/2, ψ = (1-√5)/2 satisfy φ² = φ+1 and ψ² = ψ+1 (both roots of x²-x-1=0). Binet's formula is proved by paired induction: for each n, prove fib(n) and fib(n+1) simultaneously; the recurrence step uses φ² = φ+1 to reduce φ^(n+2) to φ^n and φ^(n+1). Consequences: |ψ| < 1 (ψ → 0), nearest integer property, and φ⁵ = 5φ+3 > 10.
overview.proofStrategy:
Part I: fib_add_five by linear arithmetic from four Fibonacci recurrences. fib_five_step_growth by omega after unfolding 5 Fibonacci values. fib_ge_pow10_general by induction using fib_five_step_growth. Generalized Lamé by connecting to lame_step_bound from parent module.

Part II: phi_sq/psi_sq by ring_nf + Real.sq_sqrt. binet_pair by paired induction; inductive step uses e1/e2 exponent factoring, phi_sq/psi_sq, and ring. phi_pow5_gt_10 by computing φ⁵ = 5φ+3 and bounding φ > 7/5 from √5 > 9/5.
keyInsights: Five-step growth fib(5k+7) ≥ 10·fib(5k+2) is the direct arithmetic explanation of '5 digits'
Binet's formula shows fib(n) = round(φⁿ/√5), the nearest integer to φⁿ/√5
φ⁵ > 10: each 5 Fibonacci steps multiplies by more than 10, consuming one decimal digit
|ψ| < 1: the conjugate root ψ contributes only exponentially vanishing corrections

conclusion.summary: Unrestricted Lamé 5-digit bound + Binet's formula + φ⁵ > 10. Two complementary proofs: elementary (Part I) and golden ratio (Part II). 21 theorems, 0 axioms, 280 lines.
conclusion.implications: The connection between Fibonacci numbers, the golden ratio, and the Euclidean algorithm complexity is one of mathematics' most elegant confluences. Binet's formula shows the algorithm's worst-case behavior is governed by φ ≈ 1.618, one of the most important constants in mathematics.
openQuestions: Prove the Fibonacci zeckendorf representation: every positive integer is a unique sum of non-consecutive Fibonacci numbers
Formalize the tight worst case: the Euclidean algorithm on (fib(n+1), fib(n)) requires exactly n-1 steps
